name: @forge/trainer-mobile
_build: `expo export` is the mobile equivalent of `next build`, and it is the only step that
resolves the Metro module graph. `tsc --noEmit` type-checks files; it does not follow a
require into a package that is not a dependency, notice a missing asset, or catch a
native-only module imported from shared code. None of those are type errors, and none of
them failed anything until someone opened the app.
Both platforms, into separate directories. There is no platform-specific source in this
app today, so android and ios resolve the same graph — but the moment someone adds a
Foo.ios.tsx, a single-platform export stops covering half the code, silently. Metro
shares its transform cache between the two runs, so the second costs far less than the
first, and turbo caches the whole task anyway.
No web platform: react-native-web is not a dependency, so `--platform all` would fail.
Lives outside `scripts` because turbo requires every value in that object to be a
STRING — an array there fails package.json parsing for the whole workspace graph.

scripts.build: expo export --platform android --output-dir dist/android && expo export --platform ios --output-dir dist/ios
